title: Hidden Connections in Nature
hook: What if trees could talk to each other underground?
script: What if trees could talk to each other underground? Mushrooms connect trees and plants through hidden underground networks. These mycorrhizal connections allow them to share nutrients and even information. Can plants warn each other of threats? Research shows trees can send distress signals through these networks when attacked. They help nearby trees boost their defenses, effectively communicating in silence. Some of these networks can extend over three miles, making them among the largest living organisms on the planet. Imagine a single fungus connecting thousands of trees beneath your feet.
